payload.text: The thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery originated at the Brennecke Institute. The dopant is intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. Independent auditing corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Operation must remain at or above 4 °C, since the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte below that temperature.
